gmm.support: very strong support for two groups
gmm.verdict: ΔBIC = +637.4 (one group 18465.0, two groups 17827.6): very strong support for two groups. BIC compares Gaussian shapes, and a single skewed cloud can earn two components, so this is evidence, not proof. But its two groups are barely the DS / P-spike split (adjusted Rand 0.00, where 1 is the same split and 0 is chance; 64% of events the same): two Gaussians fit the cloud's SHAPE better than one, which a single skewed spectrum also does. Read the split-axis histogram before reading this as two populations.

rule: Pooled over 9 recordings from 9 mice, in pooled raw units: k = 1: one cluster, so no split -- every event is called DS (2183 DS, 0 P-spike, 2 not measured).

scale.why: Pooled raw units, z-scored once across the pool: differences in size between mice stay visible, impedance and placement included.
